title: Pedestrian Crossings
whatItIs: Each type of crossing works a little differently. Know who uses it and what the lights mean for you.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT park on a crossing or on its zigzag lines.
On the zigzags you MUST NOT overtake the moving vehicle nearest the crossing, or one that has stopped for pedestrians.
You MUST give way to anyone who has moved onto a zebra crossing. Give way to those waiting, too.
Flashing amber at a pelican: you MUST give way to anyone on the crossing, then go if it is clear.

keyFacts: Don't wave people across or sound your horn to hurry them: another vehicle may not stop.
In queuing traffic, keep the crossing clear.

items.title: Zebra
items.text: Black and white stripes and flashing amber beacons. No lights for traffic.

items.title: Pelican
items.text: Push-button lights. Has a flashing amber phase after the red.

items.title: Puffin
items.text: Sensors watch the crossing. No flashing amber: normal light sequence.

items.title: Toucan
items.text: Pedestrians and cyclists cross together. No flashing amber.

items.title: Equestrian
items.text: For horse riders, with higher push buttons. Often next to a toucan.

items.title: Parallel
items.text: A zebra with a cycle crossing beside it. Give way to both.

a.label: Pelican
points: Signals on the far side of the road

onTheTest.question: The amber light is flashing at a pelican crossing. What must you do?
options: Give way to anyone still on the crossing
Stop and wait for the green light
Drive on, because you have priority
Sound your horn and drive on
onTheTest.why: Flashing amber means pedestrians on the crossing still have priority. Go on only when the crossing is clear.

traps: Only pelican crossings have a flashing amber phase.
Waving someone across can lead them into the path of another vehicle.
Toucan crossings are shared with cyclists: expect bikes as well as people.
